[
  {
    "file": "packages/canvas-engine/src/components/shape-layer.tsx",
    "start": 33,
    "end": 34,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "renderer integration",
    "message": "The rotation transform is added to a renderer that the main web application does not use. At revision 719aa8340584e714552d132a9ec6971582673a8b, apps/web/src/app.tsx:48-65 registers createDomRendererPlugin() and createGpuRendererPlugin(); packages/dom-renderer/src/plugin.tsx:22-31 renders DomShapeLayer, whose wrapper has no rotation transform (packages/dom-renderer/src/dom-shape-layer.tsx:24-34). GPU rendering likewise constructs axis-aligned vertices without applying rotation (packages/gpu-renderer/src/shaders/shape-sdf.ts:33-55). Consequently, shapes remain visually unrotated in the application while the newly wrapped hit tests use rotated geometry: visible portions can become unclickable and empty regions selectable. Apply rotation to the active DOM renderer and implement GPU rotation or leave rotated shapes to a rotation-capable DOM fallback."
  },
  {
    "file": "plugins/usketch-plugin-shape-text/src/plugin.tsx",
    "start": 249,
    "end": 249,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "editing hit test",
    "message": "At revision 719aa8340584e714552d132a9ec6971582673a8b, the double-click listener still calls the raw hitTest(shape, event.worldPoint), although registration now uses withRotation(hitTest) at line 270. Thus selection and text-edit activation disagree about which points belong to rotated text. For example, a 200×28 text shape rotated 90 degrees cannot enter editing by double-clicking its visible ends outside the original horizontal bounds. The editing machine requires successive POINTER_DOWN events identifying the same shape (plugins/usketch-plugin-shape-text/src/text-editing-machine.ts:79-100), but this listener reports null there. Use the rotation-aware hit test in the editing listener as well."
  },
  {
    "file": "plugins/usketch-plugin-shape-sticky/src/plugin.tsx",
    "start": 448,
    "end": 448,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "editing hit test",
    "message": "At revision 719aa8340584e714552d132a9ec6971582673a8b, sticky-note double-click detection invokes the unwrapped hitTest directly, bypassing the rotation-aware registered hit test. For a note rotated 45 degrees, clicks on visible corners outside its original bounds do not send POINTER_DOWN to the editing service, so double-clicking those areas cannot enter editing even when selection correctly identifies the note. The editing transition requires two clicks identifying the same shape (this file:166-188). Reuse withRotation(hitTest), or the registered shape hit test, in this listener."
  }
]

[
  {
    "file": "src/lib/drive-client.ts",
    "start": 373,
    "end": 379,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "pagination",
    "message": "The name searches treat an empty first files.list page as definitive absence without requesting or following nextPageToken. Drive permits empty intermediate pages, so findFolderByName can return null for an existing folder and findOrCreateFolder then creates a duplicate. getAppDataFileByName has the same defect at lines 165–172 and can incorrectly throw DriveNotFoundError for existing JSON data. Request nextPageToken and continue searching until a match is found or pagination is exhausted."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/lib/drive-errors.ts",
    "start": 65,
    "end": 77,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "error-classification",
    "message": "Drive's HTTP 403 dailyLimitExceeded reason is missing from the quota-reason allowlist. Its standard 'Daily Limit Exceeded' message also does not match the 'rate limit' fallback, so daily API quota exhaustion becomes DrivePermissionError instead of DriveQuotaExceededError. Consumers consequently cannot distinguish exhausted API quota from missing access permissions. Include dailyLimitExceeded in the quota classification while preserving the original HTTP status."
  }
]

[
  {
    "file": "src/lib/drive-client.ts",
    "start": 373,
    "end": 378,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "pagination",
    "message": "The name searches treat an empty first page as proof that the resource does not exist, without requesting or following nextPageToken. Drive files.list can return empty partial pages even when subsequent pages contain matches. Consequently, findOrCreateFolder can create a duplicate folder instead of reusing an existing one. getAppDataFileByName has the same defect at lines 165–172 and can incorrectly throw DriveNotFoundError for existing JSON data. Request nextPageToken and continue searching until a match is found or pagination is exhausted. Evidence: src/lib/drive-client.ts at revision 876934a63ff912a060320102a818b48476a59136, lines 160–178 and 368–389."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/lib/drive-errors.ts",
    "start": 65,
    "end": 78,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "error-classification",
    "message": "The quota-reason allowlist omits Drive's dailyLimitExceeded and storageQuotaExceeded reasons. A 403 response with either reason and its normal message falls through to DrivePermissionError because the message does not contain 'rate limit'. Callers therefore cannot distinguish exhausted daily quota or full Drive storage from insufficient permissions, undermining the promised quota-error handling and leading to the wrong recovery action. Include these quota reasons in the classification. Evidence: src/lib/drive-errors.ts at revision 876934a63ff912a060320102a818b48476a59136, lines 59–80."
  }
]
